content.user_title: Configure Azure Monitor OpenTelemetry for Python
content.value_statement: Python teams need reliable Application Insights telemetry without losing control of their OpenTelemetry pipeline. This skill shows exporter setup, authentication, sampling, retry storage, and cloud-specific options.
actual_capabilities: Shows how to install the Azure Monitor OpenTelemetry exporter package.
Configures trace, metric, and log exporters for Application Insights.
Uses environment variables or explicit connection strings for exporter configuration.
Demonstrates Azure AD authentication with DefaultAzureCredential.
Explains sampling, offline storage, sovereign clouds, and exporter selection.
limitations: Does not run code, create Azure resources, or validate credentials.
Does not replace Azure security review for telemetry data handling.
Examples use placeholders and must be adapted to each environment.
Focuses on the low-level exporter, not full auto-instrumentation setup.

use_cases.title: Add Python service telemetry
use_cases.description: Set up traces, metrics, and logs from a Python service to Application Insights.

use_cases.title: Build custom observability pipelines
use_cases.description: Choose the low-level exporter when a service needs direct OpenTelemetry pipeline control.

use_cases.title: Tune production telemetry behavior
use_cases.description: Apply sampling, batch processing, retry storage, and export intervals for operational needs.

prompt_templates.title: Install the exporter
prompt_templates.prompt: Show me how to install the Azure Monitor OpenTelemetry exporter for a Python service and explain when to use it.

prompt_templates.title: Configure basic telemetry
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me configure traces, metrics, and logs for Application Insights using the Azure Monitor OpenTelemetry exporter.

prompt_templates.title: Use secure authentication
prompt_templates.prompt: Adapt the exporter setup to use Azure AD authentication and environment-based configuration instead of hardcoded connection strings.

prompt_templates.title: Design production export settings
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a production Azure Monitor exporter plan with sampling, batch processing, offline storage, sovereign cloud support, and validation steps.

output_examples.input: I need Python traces in Application Insights.
output_examples.output: A concise setup plan covering package installation, exporter choice, trace provider setup, batch processing, and validation checks.

output_examples.input: Our telemetry costs are too high.
output_examples.output: Guidance that recommends sampling, tuned export intervals, and filtering before data reaches Application Insights.
A sovereign cloud configuration plan using the correct authority host, ingestion endpoint pattern, and credential approach.

best_practices: Use Azure AD authentication when possible instead of storing instrumentation keys in source files.
Use batch processors and tuned export intervals for production workloads.
Apply sampling before export to control cost and reduce sensitive telemetry volume.
anti_patterns: Hardcoding connection strings in repositories or shared prompts.
Exporting logs that contain credentials, tokens, or personal data without filtering.
Using the low-level exporter when the Azure Monitor distro meets the need.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps configure the Azure Monitor OpenTelemetry exporter for Python traces, metrics, and logs.

faq.question: Does this skill send telemetry by itself?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples. Your application sends telemetry only after you implement exporter code.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it cover Azure AD authentication?
faq.answer: Yes. It shows DefaultAzureCredential usage for exporter authentication.

faq.question: Can it use an environment variable?
faq.answer: Yes. The exporter can read APPLICATIONINSIGHTS_CONNECTION_STRING from the environment.

faq.question: Does it cover sovereign clouds?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes an Azure Government example with a sovereign authority host and ingestion endpoint pattern.
